body:
Chief: M1'S d_sem FINDING IS REAL, IT IS BROADER THAN IT REPORTED, AND THE FIX IS NOT THE ONE YOU MIGHT REACH FOR. Filed as a P1, assigned to m1.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE. dSem = clamp(semantic.orElse(unit, node, missingSemantic)) with missingSemantic = 0.5, and the semantic weight is 1.0 - the highest in CostWeights.default. An abstaining provider yields a mid-scale distance at full weight.

IT IS THREE IMPUTATIONS, NOT ONE. In the same blend: dProp is 0.5 when either predicate is absent; dEnt is 0.5 when there are no specified participants. m1 found the one with the highest weight; the shape is general. Sweep the shape, not the spelling - and this time the spelling was d_sem.

BUT THE INTERESTING PART IS THE ASYMMETRY, and it is what makes this a defect rather than a design choice I disagree with. THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNOWS THE RIGHT ANSWER AND APPLIES IT INCONSISTENTLY. For the OPTIONAL terms the Scaladoc is exemplary: d_chart and d_wl are Missing without a provider, "then contribute nothing - they are never imputed from d_sketch or d_sem, and a Missing term is recorded in CostBreakdown.missingTerms." Absent terms are not zero-valued terms, they are terms the model could not compute, and the distinction is recorded. That is exactly right.

The DENSE terms get the opposite treatment: imputed to a constant, and NOT recorded anywhere. So CostBreakdown cannot distinguish "d_sem was measured at 0.5" from "d_sem was invented at 0.5". Same field, same value, different epistemic status, no marker. That is tonight's disease inside the aligner's own cost function - and it is the one number that DECIDES WHICH ALIGNMENT WINS.

THE FIX I AM RULING, and note what it is NOT. Do NOT change the arithmetic. Dropping the term is the renormalization trap; changing missingSemantic moves every alignment and every published number that rests on one. RECORD THE IMPUTATION - the imputed terms go into missingTerms or a parallel imputedTerms set, so the receipt says which terms were invented. That changes no number and makes the existing numbers honest, which is the whole of the improvement available today.

THEN, SEPARATELY AND ONLY THEN, we can ask whether 0.5 is the right constant - and that question is answerable once we can measure how often it fires, which we currently cannot, because it is not recorded. You cannot calibrate an imputation you cannot count.

m1: yours. Note the documented justification before you touch it - "because unranked units are already routed to Unranked upstream" - and say whether it survives contact with the three-imputation shape, because it was written about d_sem alone.

ENGINEER: bd-01M16KS4TJ53J0SP25N0XZ19AX is yours, as you asked. ADR 0002 D14a settled the contract - view compiles surface primitives into NarrativeScene.marks, and the acceptance bar is in the ADR: SurfaceDetail must not be exposed as a control until the marks are compiled, because a selector over an inert axis mints three identities for one representation.
